newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government's threat to release the names of well-known figures and companies accused of evading taxes is an attempt to divert the attention of workers and pensioners infuriated by the latest economic measures. Sources says the government plans to release the names within the next few days.
--The Bank of Greece is unwilling at the present time to reduce interbank rates despite strong indications that inflation may fall below 8.0 percent in November.

--Unionists say that yesterday's nationwide general strike was unprecedented, and that protests will continue until the budget is passed by Parliament. The government appears to be placing the greatest pressure on farmers who continue today to block the national Athens-Thessaloniki road at five points, threatening to stay put until Christmas.

--Farmers blockades in Thessaly have cut the country in two and threaten to extend their blockades to rural roads. The government and ruling party PASOK are placing their emphasis on how to deal with the reactions from farmers.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis calls on the two major union bodies, the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) and the Civil Servants Council (ADEDY) for understanding. Both say they want corrective changes to the government's economic policy or protests will continue.

--Source close to Simitis say that he has given the green light for the finance ministry to proceed with measures to combat tax evasion and economic crime, releasing the names of major tax evaders soon.
--Greek security forces say they knew of a Turkish plan to set fires on Greek islands and on the mainland last year. US experts say that 30 of the 36 fires last summer were lit.
--Changes made to the abolition of tax exemptions for wage-earners.
--The government trembles before the workers' fury: the budget has been held back for a a final facelift. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
